1.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Cryptography] What does the professor say the recovered key sheets showed about how often the Corvel cipher's substitution table changed?

options.A: It changed every week, on a fixed schedule the clerks could predict
options.B: It changed monthly, but the change was announced days later by a separate letter
options.C: It barely changed at all across the full run of years the sheets cover
options.D: It changed only when a courier reported a sheet lost or compromised

2.stem: [Academic Talk — Malacology] Why does the professor mention the water company's old filtration logs?

options.A: They record a chemical spill nowhere else documented
options.B: They rule out a suspected upstream source of the runoff
options.C: They pin down the date a specific treatment change reached this stretch
options.D: They show the company monitored this species long before any survey did

3.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Cryptography] What does the professor suggest the ongoing archive survey will let scholars do?

options.A: Cross-check the sheets' paper stock against the company's known suppliers to help date the undated ones
options.B: Fill the gap of substitution tables missing from the years the company fire affected
options.C: Establish which of the company's overseas offices received sheets first
options.D: Digitise the whole run before the fading ink makes any sheet unreadable

4.stem: [Academic Talk — Campanology] How does the professor respond to the claim that the bell's unusual tone comes from a flaw in its casting rather than its shape?

options.A: She doubts it -- an identical flaw would show up in the foundry's other bells from that year, and none do
options.B: She rejects a casting flaw but allows the bell's shape may have shifted slightly as it aged
options.C: She leans toward accepting it, citing a slight unevenness recorded during the pour
options.D: She thinks the question is open, since both the shape and a casting flaw are still on the table

5.stem: [Academic Talk — Pomology] What is the main point the professor wants to establish about the Coleraine seedling's survival?

options.A: That it very nearly did not survive a proposed grubbing in the 1980s
options.B: That it survived the 1962 frost that killed most of the orchard's other trees
options.C: That its survival owes more to a caretaker's records than to the tree itself
options.D: That it survived mainly because it stood apart from the blight that hit the rest

6.stem: [Academic Talk — Vexillology] What does the professor imply the archive project will do with the newly found flag-maker's ledger?

options.A: Match its handwriting against the harbor's own accounts to confirm which clerk kept it
options.B: Use its dye recipes to reproduce the original colors for the museum's replica set
options.C: Cross-reference the ledger's order dates against the harbor's own light-keeper's diary
options.D: Catalogue the ledger's flag-repair entries, which the harbor's own records never separately tracked

7.stem: [Academic Talk — Bryology] How does the professor respond to the idea that trampling, not drainage, explains the moss's decline near the path?

options.A: She is doubtful, since drained plots far from any path show the same decline
options.B: She thinks both play a part but that the study cannot separate their shares
options.C: She rejects it outright, pointing to plots on the path that show no decline at all
options.D: She is persuaded, since the decline stops abruptly at the same distance every year

8.stem: [Academic Talk — Bryology] What does the professor say the water-table loggers recorded this year compared with the drought year five years ago?

options.A: A shallower minimum reached later, but recovering much faster in autumn
options.B: A deeper minimum, reached in about half the time
options.C: Almost the same minimum, reached at almost the same date
options.D: A shallower minimum, but for a longer stretch of the summer

9.stem: [Academic Talk — Runology] Why does the professor mention the farmer's account of moving the Hollowmere stone in 1911?

options.A: It explains why the stone's base no longer matches its original socket
options.B: It preserves a detail about a second, smaller stone since lost
options.C: It is the only record placing the stone at its present site before 1950
options.D: It fixes the date of a churchyard clearance the stone's current plinth was built for

10.stem: [Academic Talk — Pomology] What does the professor say the trust's ledger recorded about the Coleraine seedling's original planting?

options.A: It was moved once, early on, from a nursery row to its current spot
options.B: It was the last tree planted before the orchard's boundary wall went up
options.C: It was the first tree in the orchard the trust ever fitted with a numbered tag
options.D: It was a gift tree, planted a decade after the rest of the orchard

11.stem: [Academic Talk — Campanology] Why does the professor mention the churchwarden's accounts from 1721?

options.A: They list a smaller bell sold off to help pay for the new one
options.B: They record the parish's annual payment to the foundry for the bell's general upkeep
options.C: They show the tower was strengthened before the new bell arrived
options.D: They date a dispute between the parish and the founder over the delivery date

12.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Cryptography] How does the professor respond to the claim that the Corvel cipher was broken by the rival trading company within its first year?

options.A: She accepts it, based on a rival clerk's boast that survives in one letter
options.B: She rejects it, but allows the rival broke a related, simpler cipher instead
options.C: She doubts it -- the rival's own letters keep making decisions the cipher would have prevented
options.D: She thinks it is unresolvable without letters the rival's archive no longer holds

13.stem: [Academic Talk — Ichthyology] What does the professor imply the team will do about the culvert next season?

options.A: Move the acoustic receiver array further upstream to catch fish the culvert currently hides
options.B: Tag a subset of fish with a longer-range transmitter to see where they go beyond the culvert
options.C: Ask the mill's current owner for access to open the gate during the peak weeks
options.D: Install a resting shelf partway up the culvert's inside wall

14.stem: [Academic Talk — Malacology] How does the professor respond to the idea that boat traffic, not water quality, drove the Verrow limpet's decline?

options.A: She rejects it, but allows boat wash may explain a separate, smaller local drop
options.B: She finds it convincing, since the sharpest drop follows the marina's opening
options.C: She is doubtful -- the decline began well before this stretch allowed any boats
options.D: She thinks the study cannot distinguish the two, since both changed together

15.stem: [Academic Talk — Campanology] What does the professor say the foundry's casting log recorded about the Ashcombe bell's first casting attempt?

options.A: It cracked while cooling and had to be melted down within the week
options.B: It came out true, but noticeably lighter than the order specified
options.C: It came out sound, but had to be re-poured over an error in the founder's own inscription
options.D: It was cast successfully but delayed a full season by a shortage of tin

16.stem: [Academic Talk — Ichthyology] What is the main point the professor wants to establish about the Corvane darter's migration?

options.A: That the timing of the run is set by water temperature, not day length
options.B: That most of the run's mortality happens at a single culvert, not throughout the river
options.C: That the population uses two distinct spawning grounds, not one
options.D: That the run has shifted three weeks later over the study's twenty years

17.stem: [Academic Talk — Runology] What does the professor imply the runology project will do once the raking-light survey of the region is complete?

options.A: Compare the stone's carving depth against weathering-rate data from other markers at the same site
options.B: Send a cast of the stone's final line to a specialist in a neighbouring kingdom's script for a second opinion
options.C: Cross-match the stone's line breaks against the region's known scribal training centres
options.D: Ask a stonemasons' guild archive whether any apprentice records mention working on this stone

18.stem: [Academic Talk — Vexillology] How does the professor respond to the claim that Bruntsey's flagstaff design influenced the neighboring harbor's?

options.A: She considers it an open question the surviving records cannot settle
options.B: She is unconvinced -- the neighboring harbor's staff predates Bruntsey's by several years
options.C: She agrees, but credits the shared merchant house rather than any direct copying
options.D: She finds it plausible, mainly because the same carpenter is named in both harbors' accounts

19.stem: [Academic Talk — Pomology] How does the professor respond to the claim that the Coleraine seedling is a lost cultivar rediscovered, rather than a true original?

options.A: She rejects it, but agrees the tree was likely grafted onto older rootstock
options.B: She finds it plausible, given how closely its leaf shape matches one archived cultivar
options.C: She considers it undecidable without genetic testing the trust hasn't funded
options.D: She doubts it -- its fruit chemistry doesn't match any cultivar in the regional record

20.stem: [Academic Talk — Ichthyology] Why does the professor bring up the mill records from the 1920s?

options.A: They fix the date the culvert was narrowed to its current width
options.B: They show the run was already present before the culvert existed
options.C: They record a flood that the professor uses to date a change in the channel
options.D: They document a much larger historical catch than today's population

21.stem: [Academic Talk — Campanology] What does the professor imply the conservation team will do with the bell's new laser scan?

options.A: Use the scan to plan a low-vibration cradle for the bell's next transport
options.B: Use it to recreate the bell's profile for a replica cast elsewhere
options.C: Compare the scan's acoustic model against the bell's actual recorded pitch
options.D: Share the scan data with a neighbouring parish comparing bells from the same founder

22.stem: [Academic Talk — Ichthyology] What does the professor say the acoustic tags showed about fish that passed the culvert at night?

options.A: They cleared it faster, but arrived at the spawning ground in poorer condition
options.B: They took nearly twice as long to clear it as fish that passed by day
options.C: They doubled back below the culvert far more often than daytime fish
options.D: They were no more likely to be lost from the record than daytime fish

23.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Cryptography] Why does the professor mention the ledger clerk's marginal doodles?

options.A: They show the clerk was distracted, which the professor uses to explain an error
options.B: They are unrelated, and the professor mentions them only as an aside
options.C: One doodle turns out to be a partial key, copied down where it shouldn't be
options.D: They date the ledger to a specific quarter by referencing a known event

24.stem: [Academic Talk — Runology] What does the professor say the new raking-light photographs showed about the stone's final line?

options.A: That what earlier readers took for damage was in fact a deliberate erasure
options.B: A short phrase that matches a formula found on two other stones in the region
options.C: That the line was added later, in a noticeably different hand
options.D: Traces of a name where earlier readings had seen only an ornamental border

25.stem: [Academic Talk — Malacology] What does the professor imply the team will do next to build on the filtration evidence?

options.A: Place limpet cages just below the treatment outflow and monitor them through a full season
options.B: Send a batch of shells for isotope testing to see what the water carried when they grew
options.C: Ask a neighbouring catchment's water company for its own filtration logs, to see whether the pattern repeats there
options.D: Ask the water company for the outflow's daily readings instead of the logged averages

26.stem: [Academic Talk — Vexillology] Why does the professor mention Bruntsey Roads' 1888 pilot-boat log?

options.A: It lists the toll charged to fishing boats using the harbor's new pilot steps
options.B: It records the original height of the harbor's signal mast, later found to be inaccurate
options.C: A damaged page in it dates a storm that later accounts disagree about
options.D: It notes a shipment of replacement flags lost overboard before it ever reached the harbor

27.stem: [Academic Talk — Pomology] What does the professor suggest the Marrow Hill orchard trust will do once the graft trial concludes?

options.A: Retire the trial's weakest grafts and free the block for a second generation of cuttings
options.B: Replant the trial block using only rootstock from the orchard's own oldest tree
options.C: Send wood samples from each surviving graft for a rootstock compatibility trial
options.D: Release scion wood from the surviving grafts to other heritage orchards

28.stem: [Academic Talk — Vexillology] What is the main point the professor wants to establish about the flag changeover?

options.A: That confusion during the changeover caused at least one recorded near-collision
options.B: That it was driven by a naval order, not a local harbor decision
options.C: That the old and new codes were briefly used together on purpose
options.D: That it happened gradually, flag by flag, rather than on a single date

29.stem: [Academic Talk — Runology] How does the professor respond to the claim that the Hollowmere stone commemorates a voyage rather than a death?

options.A: She doubts it -- the stone's opening line names the deceased using a formula reserved for burials
options.B: She finds it plausible, since the stone's carving style matches others raised for departures rather than deaths
options.C: She thinks the text alone cannot settle it, and no other evidence survives
options.D: She rejects it, but agrees the named river points to an unusually well-traveled family

30.stem: [Academic Talk — Bryology] Why does the professor mention the moss samples kept in the university herbarium since the 1950s?

options.A: Their collection dates mark the last time the moss covered the whole bog
options.B: They show the moss was already a paler shade than field guides of the time describe
options.C: They let the team check whether today's moss is the same species as before
options.D: They record a decade when the moss was surveyed by a different, now-retired botanist

31.stem: [Academic Talk — Bryology] What does the professor suggest the team will change about next year's plots on Hallow Moss?

options.A: Move the growth measurement to a later date, since this year's readings ran early
options.B: Fence two plots to keep deer off them and see whether growth recovers
options.C: Mark a fresh set of plots along the moss's eastern boundary, where last year's team never sampled
options.D: Add a set of plots on the moss's shaded, north-facing edge for comparison

32.stem: [Academic Talk — Malacology] What does the professor say the shell-growth bands showed about limpets from the slower side-channel versus the main current?

options.A: Side-channel limpets grew steadily slower across every year in the record
options.B: The two groups grew at about the same rate until the last five years
options.C: Side-channel limpets grew faster in most years but slower in drought years
options.D: Main-current limpets grew faster, but only in shells collected before the current logging equipment was installed
